question: Do wider repeated not-all-equal meetings preserve reconstruction of full states and next ordinary births from uniform pair disagreement rates?
primary_observable: Exact scoped pair tables, states and next counts across both ages; local recoverability by repeated meetings or declared finite dictionary; fresh first- and second-stage membership by law.
forbidden_inputs: Using hidden ages, labels of parts, word count or source identity as given pair data; treating exact invariant equality as isomorphism or a structural cohort as universal.
cheapest_meaningful_control: Literal bare (4,4) overlaps 3 and 2, mixed (4,5), parity and actual first child rows; single-name and disjoint controls.
first_executable_signal: Bare two-holder complete-word check followed by ordinary growth under both laws, then second reached and width-nine-to-ten census gates.
resource_budget: 6 GiB per process, one BLAS thread, width limits and tensor ceiling 3^12 per factor; prior notification/registration of any ≥10min check; 128 fresh draws per weighting and law.
stop_rule: Live equal-rate NAE case with distinct next counts, theorem for every reached case, or the certified census bounds with strongest proved structural class and all remaining cases explicit.
decision_or_followup_rule: Distinguish named states vs scalar births, conditional proof vs unrestricted alternatives, full census vs affordability, law vs sampling, and independent referee pending.
